It represents roughly the same sound in both alphabets: in Modern Greek, a somewhat lowered variant of the mid front unrounded vowel: /e/ or /e̞/. It is preceded by δ (d) and followed in the archaic alphabet by ϝ (w) and in the classical alphabet by ζ (z).

grc:other:Ε.gloss: The letter now called epsilon (ἒ ψιλόν (è psilón)), the fifth letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.
